requirement:
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.

For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`.

- **Successful read records identity and fingerprint (Rust caller).**
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]` asserts `dependencies()` equals `Dependency::Node(node, fp(original))` after `read_snapshot`. It uses empty and multi-page Unicode contents.
  - `fn[snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions]` asserts the same for `read`. It also asserts that the later read with different content adds a second `Dependency::Node` for the same node with the "after" fingerprint, so both observations are kept.
- **Failed read records no successful observation.**
  - `fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]` reads missing node 9 and asserts the error is `"missing"` and `dependencies()` is empty.
  - `fn[snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions]` reads missing node 2 and asserts it adds no entry.
- **Staleness when a later read has a different fingerprint.**
  - Both direct-read tests assert `record.is_current(...)` is false after the contents change.
  - The `is_current` check is outside this requirement. Failure to resolve a dependency is delegated to `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`, which is cited and not reassessed here.
- **Agent delivery semantics.**
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery]` checks that a `read_node` result delivered through a successful provider response records the node and the full-content fingerprint. It also checks that when the provider fails after a prepared `read_node`, `dependencies()` is empty. The usage counters (prepared 6, delivered 4) separate preparation from delivery.
  - `fn[graph_read_pages_retain_the_prepared_snapshot_after_contents_change]` mirrors the requirement's example. `ChangingProvider::complete` replaces the node's contents on the request that carries the tool result, before the provider responds. The test asserts that the recorded fingerprint equals the original contents and that the graph was read only once. It also asserts that the pages delivered to the model add up to the original text.
  - `fn[node_preparation_tool_errors_allow_recovery_without_recording_undelivered_contents]` shows that a tool error from node preparation records no observation, though the error itself is delivered.
  - `fn[concurrent_tool_agents_isolate_histories_pages_and_submissions_and_share_reads]` adds a check that observations from concurrent agents are recorded correctly.

I found no gap and no marking gap.

:::{req} node_inputs
Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
:::{req} checking_records
The method is declared under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.check_inputs`.
The method resolves the recorded dependencies through graph operations and
fingerprinting, comparing each with its saved observation. A fingerprint
mismatch returns `Ok(false)` and permits an early return; it need not resolve
later dependencies. An encountered dependency-resolution failure returns an
error.
The method observes the current state that the caller intends to inspect.
Freshness checking has a separate observation scope from criterion execution.
Checked observations enter the new trace when execution explicitly reads
or delivers them.
A checked snapshot can be reused if it still represents the current state.
